text:
Jiri Kulich's season has turned. In October the question was whether Buffalo might send him to the AHL to find his game. Now he's on the top line with Tage Thompson and Zach Benson, and the headlines say he's hitting his stride. He has scored in back-to-back games, including a breakaway goal off a neutral-zone pick, and Joe Yerdon wrote that it's "great to see Kulich getting rewarded."

He has four goals and seven points in 16 games at 14:23 a night. The underlying play is better than the line: Buffalo takes 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 6.7 points better than without him. His finishing is right on his chances, four goals on 4.5 expected. He has no power-play points yet, which is where more production could come from. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, so this is a real step. Our range projects 25 to 47 points, wide because his role is still settling.
